subject: Communication Systems
questionText:
Common data for Q.10 and 11: 
 
Consider a 18000 meter twisted-pair telephone line 
having a usable bandwidth of 750 kHz. 
 
 
10. What is the maximum data rate that can be supported 
on this line to produce a null to null bandwidth of 750 
kHz, if QPSK signaling with a signal carrier is used? 
 
(a) 
1125 kbps 
(b) 750 kbps 
 
(c) 
500 kbps 
(d) 373 kbps 
 
11. If OFDM signaling with QPSK carriers is used then 
the maximum data rate that can be supported on this 
line to produce a null bandwidth of 750 kHz is 
 
(a) 
1.5 Mbps 
(b) 750 kbps 
 
(c) 
3 Mbps 
(d) 375 kbps 
 
 
Common data Q.12 and 13: 
 
Assume that a telephone line channel is equalized to 
allow bandpass data transmission over a frequency 
range of 400 to 3100 Hz. So that the available channel 
bandwidth is 2700 Hz and the midchannel frequency 
is 1750 Hz. A 16 symbol QAM signaling scheme is 
designed such that it allows a data rate of 9600 bits/s 
to be transferred over the channel.
explanation: Practice Question from Communication Systems DPP-06 (PRACTICE SHEET 01).
